title: applied-ml-experiment-scratchpad
content:
Daily scratchpad — Applied ML experiments (feb 24 -> mar 3)

Goals
- Quick iter loop for quantized inference quality vs latency on candidate models for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) use cases.
- Finalize prompt set and baseline evals to compare int8/awq/qat profiles.
- Surface a small set of recommended configs for Redwood Dedicated to test under realistic concurrent loads.

High-level notes
- Target models: llama-2-13b-chat, meta-llama-7b, and mosaicml/mpt-7b-instruct (for diversity).
- Quant libs: bitsandbytes (bnb-int8), AWQ (per-token 4-bit), and ggml fallback for local CPU checks.
- Primary eval sets: openai_eval_qa_small (500 queries), synthetic_prompt_set_v2 (200 prompts focusing on instruction-following), and retrieval_sim_100 (RAG-like).

Quick todo
- [x] seed synthetic_prompt_set_v2 and upload to S3 (s3://redwood-expts/prompt-sets/v2) — 2026-02-24
- [x] baseline FP16 runs on hosted infra (latency & token-cost) — 2026-02-25
- [ ] run AWQ 4-bit for llama-2-13b and record top-1 acceptance rate threshold — due 2026-03-04
- [ ] run concurrent 8-client throughput test w/ kv-cache warm (Dedicated sim) — due 2026-03-05
- [ ] assemble a one-slide summary for eng-sync with perf numbers and recommended defaults

Experiment log (selected)
- 2026-02-25: baseline FP16 (llama-2-13b-chat)
  * dataset: openai_eval_qa_small (500)
  * avg latency/token (seq len ~128): 12.8 ms
  * p95 latency: 42 ms
  * avg tokens generated: 75
  * acceptance/accuracy (exact-match-like metric): 0.72
  * notes: stable, good quality baseline to compare quantized runs.

- 2026-02-26: BNB int8 (bitsandbytes) on llama-2-13b-chat
  * config: bnb 8-bit (default), no further calibration
  * avg latency/token: 7.4 ms
  * p95 latency: 28 ms
  * accuracy: 0.69 (-0.03 vs fp16)
  * artifacts: /artifacts/bnb-llama2-13b-20260226/checkpoint (uploaded)
  * notes: small drop in correctness on few instruction-heavy q's (see examples).

- 2026-03-01: AWQ 4-bit per-channel quant (llama-2-13b-chat)
  * config: awq-perchannel-4bit, act-ordering: stable
  * avg latency/token: 5.9 ms
  * p95 latency: 22 ms
  * accuracy: 0.66 (-0.06 vs fp16)
  * weird failure: hallucination on followup Q#37 in openai_eval_qa_small (investigate prompt ctx truncation)
  * notes: very promising latency improvement, but regression in edge cases — try tiny calibration set for AWQ.

- 2026-03-02: AWQ w/ tiny calibration (100 samples from eval)
  * accuracy: 0.685 (+0.025 vs awq-no-calib)
  * avg latency/token: 6.1 ms (small overhead)
  * conclusion: calibration helps recover ~40% of quality delta, worth including as default step.

Prompt set (working)
- prompt_v2_instruct_01: "You are a helpful assistant. Answer concisely in 2-3 sentences. If uncertain, say \"I don't know\" and propose one plausible next step."
- prompt_v2_rag_01: retrieval context appended as triple-dashed block. Ensure you prioritize facts from context, then generalize.
- testing notes: ensure system-role included when running chat endpoints (some model variants show tokenization differences if system role missing).

Known issues / observations
- Tokenization mismatch: mosaicml/mpt-7b-instruct shows ~2 token higher avg for same prompts vs llama family. Account for in cost calc.
- AWQ per-channel sometimes exposes range-clipping artifacts on very long tails — add a post-quantization verify (run 50 synthetic edge prompts).
- BNB-int8 is easiest to deploy on current infra; AWQ has better perf but adds calibration/complexity. Might recommend AWQ for Dedicated where we can persist calibration artifacts.

Commands / reproducibility notes
- baseline fp16 run (container): python run_eval.py --model llama2-13b-chat --precision fp16 --dataset openai_eval_qa_small --out ./out/fp16-baseline.json
- bnb int8: python run_eval.py --model llama2-13b-chat --quant bnb8 --dataset openai_eval_qa_small --out ./out/bnb8-20260226.json
- awq: python run_eval.py --model llama2-13b-chat --quant awq-4 --calib_samples 0 --out ./out/awq-no-calib.json
- awq + calib: python run_eval.py --model llama2-13b-chat --quant awq-4 --calib_samples 100 --out ./out/awq-calib-100.json

Metrics to track (final slide)
- avg latency/token (ms)
- p95 latency (ms)
- throughput @ N concurrent clients
- cost per 1k tokens (est)
- delta accuracy vs fp16 (absolute points)

Next steps
- Run AWQ + 500-sample calibration and the concurrent 8-client throughput sim (Dedicated config)
- Start a short ablation: AWQ per-channel vs per-tensor on 7b models (spot-check quality)
- Draft ops checklist for deploying AWQ model variants: calibration artifact storage, verification harness, fallback rules to bnb-int8 if quality below threshold.

Notes to self (misc)
- Remember to add a small note in PR (GH-PR-4123) about the seed for calibration (so runs are reproducible).
- Ping SRE (Marco) about testing Dedicated autoscaling scenario when running concurrent throughput tests.

Examples of failure cases (copied snippets)
- Q37 (openai_eval_qa_small): prompt: "How would you summarize this product for a non-technical user?"
  * FP16: "It helps teams run LLMs with predictable latency and cost."
  * AWQ-no-calib: "It uses GPUs to store your data and returns an opinionated summary about pricing."
  * action: isolate prompt, run token-level trace to see context tokens dropped.

++ end of scratchpad ++
